findings.summary: The plan says it counts auditor (and steward/audience) runs toward the class of the job they serve. Real records never have that shape, so the main 'fails without the behavior' proof depends on a fixture production never writes.
findings.evidence: Read crates/athena-core/src/auditor.rs:338: `let run_job = JobId::Id(RecordId::generate(now));`. The auditor's invocation carries a newly generated id, not the audited job's id. steward.rs:1239 and audience.rs:238 do the same. store.rs:429-437 sends these runs to auditor_runs, steward_runs and audience_runs by role. So no real out-of-job run carries a classed job's id, and reading all_invocations() adds nothing over jobs[..].invocations. The plan's discriminator ('If compute read only jobs[..].invocations, docs would be 3500/3 and the 1200.0 assertion fails') rests only on the hand-made auditor run tagged to d2. reading/surveys.rs:494-501 records this same root cause: records measures checked on fixtures 'held the shapes the author expected, so a wrong figure showed only on the real records.' D175 would also write the false claim into the decision log. Fix: State the true behavior: steward, audience and auditor runs carry their own generated ids and are charged to no class. Change the core fixture so the auditor run has its own generated-style id, and assert it is not counted (docs = 3500 tokens over 3 landed jobs, or adjust the constants). Base the 'fails without' proof on behaviors that exist: output tokens excluded, and a lower-bound quantity counted at its lower bound. Reading all_invocations() can stay for robustness, but Decision 3 and D175 must not claim it captures auditor work per class. If the auditor's cost per audited job is wanted, join it through the Audit record that names the job and test it with a record shape auditor.rs actually writes.

findings.summary: The figures are only ever checked against hand-built fixtures, a pattern the codebase records as having produced wrong status figures before.
findings.evidence: surveys.rs:494-501 records that the status landing time was wrong twice (0.1 and then 273.8 minutes) because only fixtures were checked. The plan has no records branch and leaves the real-records check to the owner after landing. Fix: Keep the cli test seeding through the real records loader, as planned. In D175, state explicitly which invocation kinds are and are not counted, and list a real-records sanity check as a named follow-up rather than leaving it implicit.

findings.summary: The mistake count is an all-time raw count by intervention class, shown next to figures that cover only closed jobs. The two have different scopes, and a raw count grows with volume.
findings.evidence: status.rs:600-602 counts every mistake intervention by its class_of_work, with no link to a closed job. The landed share and tokens per landed job use only closed request jobs. A class with more jobs will show more mistakes even when its outcomes held equally well. Fix: State the scope in the line text or D175. Alternatively, show mistakes per closed job next to the raw count so classes can be compared.

summary: The plan fits the accepted reading. The modules, labels and functions it names exist where it says: STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS at status.rs:305, the label/field/printed-line test at status.rs:1689, mistake_report at status.rs:595, trend_section at display.rs:1103, and the ci_shards timings check at ci_shards.rs:411. The extra cli test and the shard-timings lines are justified. One design premise is wrong: the plan claims to count auditor runs toward the audited job's class and makes that the main 'fails without' proof in its core test. But auditor.rs:338, steward.rs:1239 and audience.rs:238 tag their runs with newly generated ids, so real records never have that shape, and D175 would record a false claim. This is the fixture-only failure the codebase warns about in surveys.rs:494-501. Fixing the fixture and the decision text is a small revision. Two minor points: the figures are not checked on real records, and the all-time mistake count has a different scope from the closed-job figures.
